standard.title: Create and communicate content
standard.description: use the basic features of common digital tools to create, locate and communicate content
standard.prior_knowledge: This is the first content creation descriptor (no Foundation predecessor). Students have used digital systems in familiar contexts and can recognise what they are used for. They have not yet deliberately used digital tools to create original content, locate specific content, or communicate content to others.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use basic features of common digital tools to create original content, locate relevant content, and communicate that content to others.

nodes.label: Using basic features to create content
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use the basic features of a common digital tool to create a piece of content
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one basic feature of a digital tool (camera, drawing app, text input, presentation software) to create a piece of original content
nodes.typical_width: Use basic features across different content types (take a photo, draw a picture, type a message, add text to a presentation) using appropriate tools; save or store the created content
wider: Use presentation software to retell a story — apply features to combine text and pictures to communicate the story sequence
Create a card for a family member using a camera or drawing app — include a photo and a short typed message, combining two creation features

response_modes.reason: Feature use at this level requires motor accuracy and procedural memory — selecting the right icon, saving correctly, locating saved work. Students need repeated practice with the same features across multiple creation tasks before fluency develops. Consolidation here prevents stalling on procedural steps when communicating content.

success_criteria: Uses at least one basic feature of a digital tool to produce original content
The content produced is accessible — saved or stored so it can be found again
nodes.hinge_reason: Procedural fluency with creation features is prerequisite for Node 2 — students who stall on feature access during creation cannot redirect attention to locating and retrieving content.

nodes.label: Using basic features to locate content
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use the basic features of a digital tool to locate specific content — including stored files and online images
nodes.minimum_width: Use a basic feature of a digital tool to locate one piece of stored or online content relevant to a task (e.g. find a saved photo, find an image of a plant or animal)
nodes.typical_width: Locate stored files (photos of their own work) and find images online for a purpose (local flora and fauna, places); explain how they found the content and what they used it for
wider: Find images of Australian flora and fauna including First Nations Australians' names for the items — use the images in a story or presentation, crediting the source
Take photos of class work and locate them in a class shared folder — demonstrate that stored content can be found and used again later

response_modes.reason: Locating content involves navigating file systems, folders and browser interfaces — procedural skills that require accurate execution. Students commonly lose their saved content or cannot find it again. Repeated practice locating and retrieving content builds the navigational fluency needed for subsequent communication tasks.

success_criteria: Locates at least one piece of content (stored file or online image) relevant to the task
Can show or explain where the content was found
nodes.hinge_reason: Content that cannot be located cannot be communicated — Node 3 requires students to find and organise content before sharing it. Navigational failure at Node 2 collapses the Node 3 communication task.

nodes.label: Using basic features to communicate content
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use the basic features of a digital tool to communicate created or located content to others
nodes.minimum_width: Use a digital tool to share or present a piece of content to at least one other person (show a photo, present a slide, share a message)
nodes.typical_width: Create individual content contributions that form part of a group task — for example contributing a recipe and photo to a class recipe book; present or share completed content with the class or a family member
wider: Contribute a recipe and photo of a favourite food to a class digital recipe book — explain how individual contributions combine to create a shared piece of content
Use presentation software to show class work on an interactive display — explain what the content shows and respond to feedback

response_modes.reason: Communication requires students to coordinate creation (produce content), location (find or organise it) and presentation (share it with others). At this node, the three activities — create, locate, communicate — must work together. Integration failure looks like: content exists but cannot be found to share, or content is shared but is incomplete or unintended.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The class recipe book direction is genuinely rich — individual contributions that form a shared whole surface the concept of collaborative digital production. This goes beyond minimum communication to purposeful content creation and collection.
success_criteria: Communicates content to at least one other person using a digital tool
The content shared is the intended content — not accidentally shared, not the wrong file
